candidates.title: Turn monthly review decks into video drafts

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a narrated video draft from a monthly review deck for a team, investor, or client.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: if you send your team, your investors or your clients a review deck every month

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable narrated video draft made from an operator-supplied monthly review deck.
inputs: Synthetic monthly review deck with fictional figures
Operator-supplied audience and brand color choices
Operator-supplied narration and video service credentials
experimentPlan.trigger: A consultant starts a test after receiving a monthly review deck.
steps: Read the supplied deck and audience notes.
Draft a short narration using only the supplied figures.
Prepare a video render request for a configured test service.
Render a draft and show it beside the source deck.
Ask a person to check every figure and approve any sharing.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fictional deck, verify every number in the narration against its source slide and confirm the draft video uses the selected audience and branding.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies the deck and credentials, checks the rendered video and figures, and authorizes any client or investor sharing.
unverified: Correct extraction from varied deck formats
Video service access, cost, and render reliability
Whether review teams would pay for this proposed service

ease.reason: The retained context describes an importable workflow but requires configured keys, local files, and manual execution.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: consultants or small firms preparing monthly reviews might pay for video preparation; this post shows no payment intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sample-deck prototype is bounded, but rendering needs a third-party key and the supplied steps do not establish reliable output.

autonomy.reason: The post describes repeatable generation steps, but the operator supplies files and keys and must check the render.

evidence.reason: The task span identifies monthly review decks and the retained context gives setup steps; broader demand and buyer intent are unverified.

candidates.reason: Below six: concrete monthly task but buyer intent, output quality, and reliable rendering are not established.

candidates.title: Review replies that include a product image

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a draft product-identification reply using a customer message and an image already supplied to the workflow.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Customers can send either text messages or images.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable reply draft that acknowledges an already supplied product image and asks only for missing details.
inputs: Operator-written list of known product names
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator starts a test when a sample message arrives with an image.
steps: Pair the message with its supplied image in a test record.
Ask a multimodal model for a cautious product description.
Compare the description with the operator supplied product list.
Draft a reply that marks uncertain identification.
Have a person verify the image and approve or rewrite the reply.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On fictional message-image pairs, check that the draft never asks to resend an image already present and marks any uncertain product match for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person provides the test pair, verifies image interpretation and product identity, and approves every response; no customer message is sent automatically.
unverified: A suitable image-capable model and its handling of supplied images
Reliable pairing of image and message in the actual Make scenario
Whether preventing repeat image requests is frequent enough to pay for

ease.reason: A fictional message-image pair can support a manual mock, but no attached reference documents image handoff or interpretation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online sellers might pay to reduce repeat image requests; this single question establishes no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A draft-only sample is possible, but using image content correctly depends on unsupported multimodal handling.

autonomy.reason: A person must supply the pair, verify product identification, and approve any reply; no routing or execution support is attached.

evidence.reason: The retained post describes text and image routes and the repeated resend issue, but this is one case with no corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below six: the specific repeat-image problem is stated, but the required image interpretation and Make handoff capabilities are unsupported in supplied references.

candidates.title: Turn rough sketches into wireframe drafts

demandEvidence.chore: Convert a rough iPad sketch into a higher-fidelity wireframe or illustration draft.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: translate rough sketches on my iPad to higher fidelity wireframes or illustrations in near real time

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable wireframe draft based on one operator-supplied rough sketch.
inputs: Operator description of intended screen purpose
Operator-selected list of required interface elements
experimentPlan.trigger: A designer starts a test after choosing a sketch for conversion.
steps: Load the sketch and the designer notes.
Ask an image-capable model for a structured layout description.
Convert the description into a simple wireframe draft.
Show the draft beside the original sketch.
Have a designer correct structure and confirm it is usable.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each fictional sketch, compare the draft with the designer supplied required elements and record missing or invented elements before judging usefulness.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A designer supplies the sketch and requirements, reviews the generated layout for omissions and inventions, and decides whether to use it.
unverified: Access to a suitable image-to-layout model
Reliable conversion from varied sketches into editable wireframes
Whether near-real-time output is achievable and useful

ease.reason: A student could test fictional sketches, but no supplied reference documents sketch ingestion or image transformation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent designers may pay for faster sketch-to-wireframe drafts; this request does not establish payment intent.

feasibility.reason: The central image-to-wireframe transformation is unsupported by supplied implementation evidence, so a useful four-week version is uncertain.

autonomy.reason: A person must provide sketches and judge every generated layout; no repeatable supported transformation is documented.

evidence.reason: The request states a specific sketch-to-wireframe task and near-real-time preference, but gives no workflow details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below six: the task is explicit, but the core transformation is unsupported and the post gives no input, workflow, or quality criteria.
